entries.facts: AB 468 (2021), Health & Safety Code §122318, effective January 1, 2022: a health care practitioner may provide emotional support animal documentation only if they hold a valid active license, are licensed in the jurisdiction, established a client-provider relationship at least 30 days before issuing the documentation, and completed a clinical evaluation. Online certificates with no individualized assessment are presumptively not reliable third-party information under California housing regulations.
entries.currencyNote: Verified current 2026-08-10 against the chaptered bill text on leginfo. HUD's May 22, 2026 FHEO enforcement memo narrowed FEDERAL enforcement to trained animals only; it does not change AB 468 or California's untrained-support-animal standard, which CRD enforces independently.

entries.facts: Oxnard's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (Ordinance 3013, City Code ch. 27, adopted 2022) limits covered units to one rent increase per 12-month period, capped at 4%. It covers multifamily residential property first issued a certificate of occupancy before February 1, 1995; most single-family homes and condominiums are exempt (see §27-24(B)(3)), consistent with Costa-Hawkins. Oxnard also runs a mandatory rental registry and separate just-cause protections (Ordinance 3012).
entries.currencyNote: Verified current 2026-08-10 against the City of Oxnard rent stabilization page. Registration was required by April 1, 2025; a 2026 fee study proposes per-unit program fees. Local ordinances change — re-check the city page before relying on figures.

entries.facts: AB 1482 caps annual rent increases for covered units at 5% plus regional CPI, or 10%, whichever is LOWER, over any 12-month period. Adds just-cause eviction protection. Remains in effect until January 1, 2030.

entries.facts: A nonpayment eviction begins with a 3-day Notice to Pay Rent or Quit (at least 3 days, excluding weekends and judicial holidays). If unpaid after it expires, the landlord may file an Unlawful Detainer action; the tenant cannot be removed without a court judgment and sheriff lockout.
entries.currencyNote: Verified current 2026-06-25. SB 436 (2025-26), which would have extended the notice to 14 days, FAILED passage in committee, so the 3-day period remains current law. Re-check if reintroduced.

entries.facts: Emotional support animals are assistance animals under the federal Fair Housing Act and California FEHA, not pets. Housing providers must grant a reasonable accommodation regardless of a no-pet policy, and may NOT charge a pet deposit or pet rent for an assistance animal. Accommodation can be denied only if the specific animal is a direct threat or would cause substantial property damage. Online 'ESA certificates' alone are not sufficient documentation.
entries.currencyNote: Verified current 2026-06-25 against CA CRD ESA FAQ and HUD assistance-animal guidance.

entries.facts: California caps the tenant application screening fee at a statutory maximum that began at $30 (1998) and is adjusted annually by the Consumer Price Index, and the fee may not exceed the landlord's actual out-of-pocket screening costs plus reasonable time. The landlord must provide a receipt itemizing the out-of-pocket expenses.
entries.currencyNote: Verified current 2026-06-25 against Civ. Code 1950.6. The 'actual out-of-pocket cost only' rule is PROPOSED in SB 381 (2025-26), NOT yet law — do not state it as current. Re-check the CPI-adjusted dollar cap annually.

entries.facts: IRC §121 lets you exclude up to $250,000 of gain ($500,000 married filing jointly) on the sale of a main home if you owned AND used it as your main home for at least 2 of the 5 years before the sale. Gain attributable to depreciation taken while it was a rental is NOT excludable (depreciation recapture). You generally can't use the exclusion twice within 2 years.
entries.currencyNote: Verified current 2026-06-25 against IRS Topic 701 / Pub. 523 (2025).

entries.facts: IRC §1031 defers gain when business/investment real property is exchanged for like-kind business/investment real property. Since the TCJA it applies to real property only. To avoid receipt of proceeds you must use a safe harbor such as a qualified intermediary. Strict timelines: identify replacement property within 45 days and close within 180 days. U.S. property is not like-kind to foreign property.
entries.currencyNote: Verified current 2026-06-25 against IRS like-kind exchanges guidance.

sources.label: IRS, Like-Kind Exchanges — Real Estate Tax Tips

entries.facts: AB 2801 amends Cal. Civ. Code §1950.5 to add photo-documentation duties. From April 1, 2025, a landlord who deducts from the deposit for repairs/cleaning must take photos before and after the work and include them, with a written cost explanation, in the itemized statement. From July 1, 2025, landlords must also take move-in photos. The 21-day return deadline is unchanged.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. Phased effective dates (Apr 1, 2025 deduction photos; Jul 1, 2025 move-in photos) confirmed. Amends §1950.5.

entries.facts: Cal. Civ. Code §1950.5 governs residential security deposits: the landlord must return the deposit and an itemized statement of deductions within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent, cleaning to the level of cleanliness at move-in, and repair of damage beyond ordinary wear and tear. Subdivision (f) gives the tenant a pre-move-out (initial) inspection right and a chance to cure before move-out.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. Long-standing statute; deposit cap changes via AB 12 (eff. Jul 1, 2024) and photo duties via AB 2801.

sources.label: California Security Deposit Law, Cal. Civ. Code Section 1950.5

entries.facts: AB 628 amends Cal. Civ. Code §1941.1 to add a working refrigerator and a working stove to the conditions required for a dwelling to be habitable. Effective January 1, 2026, it applies to tenancies entered into or renewed on or after that date, NOT automatically to every existing occupied unit. A tenant may supply their own refrigerator only by mutual written agreement (revocable, triggering a 30-day landlord-replace window); there is no tenant opt-out for the stove. Certain housing (SRO, residential hotels, communal-kitchen facilities) is exempt under §1941.1(b).
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. Effective Jan 1, 2026 for leases entered/renewed on/after that date. Confirm exact subdivision + exemptions against the final chaptered text.

entries.facts: Cal. Civ. Code §1941.1 lists the conditions that make a residential dwelling untenantable under the implied warranty of habitability — effective waterproofing/weather protection, working plumbing and hot/cold water, adequate heating, safe electrical, and clean, sanitary premises free of vermin and debris. Mold, water intrusion, and smoke/ash intrusion can breach it. AB 628 (eff. Jan 1, 2026) adds a working refrigerator and stove.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. Long-standing statute; amended by AB 628 for 2026.

entries.facts: California AB 325 (effective January 1, 2026) amends the Cartwright Act (adds Bus. & Prof. Code §16729) to target a 'common pricing algorithm' — a shared methodology that uses competitor data to align or set prices — and lowers the pleading standard. Using an algorithm on ONLY your own data is clearly permissible; whether the law reaches publicly available competitor data is legally unresolved, so do not state that using public comps in a shared tool is definitively safe. Separately, the U.S. DOJ sued RealPage on Aug. 23, 2024 under the Sherman Act for algorithmic price coordination using competitors' nonpublic data.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. AB 325 effective Jan 1, 2026. NUANCE: public-vs-nonpublic competitor-data reach is unsettled — only own-data use is clearly safe. RealPage case ongoing (allegation).

entries.facts: Cal. SB 610 (effective January 1, 2026; adds Civ. Code §§1941.8 and 1941.9) is a DISASTER-specific tenant-protection statute tied to a declared emergency and the landlord's failure to repair disaster damage in time. Where the landlord fails to repair, the tenant may notify the landlord, terminate the tenancy, vacate, and be discharged from further obligations, with prepaid rent returned; the security deposit is returned under §1950.5. It is not a general 'any uninhabitable unit' termination law — the general right to quit an untenantable dwelling is Civ. Code §1933(4)/§1942.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. Disaster-specific, effective Jan 1, 2026. Attribute deposit return to §1950.5.

entries.facts: The Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, Cal. Civ. Code §1954.50 et seq., exempts single-family homes/condos and units first occupied after Feb. 1, 1995 from local rent control and guarantees vacancy decontrol (an owner may reset rent to market for a new tenancy after a prior tenant voluntarily leaves or is lawfully evicted). It limits the reach of local rent-control ordinances but not AB 1482's statewide cap.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. Long-standing statute (1995).

sources.label: Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, Cal. Civ. Code §1954.50

entries.facts: SOAR (Save Open-space and Agricultural Resources) is a set of Ventura County voter initiatives requiring a public vote before designated open-space, agricultural, or rural land is rezoned for urban development. Voters extended the county measure in 2016, now running through 2050; several cities have their own SOAR/urban-boundary measures. By constraining where new housing can be built, SOAR is frequently cited as a factor limiting Ventura County housing supply.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09 via Ventura County RMA. County measure through 2050; confirm the specific jurisdiction for city-level claims.

entries.facts: A California real estate broker/agent owes the principal (owner/landlord) a fiduciary duty of utmost care, integrity, honesty, and loyalty (Cal. Civ. Code §2079.16), plus the duties of an agent under §2079.13 and the actual-authority limits of §2316. A property manager has authority over day-to-day operations but must bring any decision that exposes the owner to a new category of risk — a non-ordinary use, an offer, an enforcement operation — to the owner for an informed decision, and must present all offers.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. Long-standing agency/fiduciary statutes; the 'present all offers' duty is reinforced by DRE regulation and common law.

entries.facts: Under California law a buyer takes title subject to an existing lease: a valid fixed-term lease survives the sale and binds the new owner for the remaining term (the purchaser steps into the landlord's shoes; Civ. Code §821). Rent increases on a month-to-month tenancy follow Civ. Code §827 — at least 30 days' written notice for an increase of 10% or less in a 12-month period, and 90 days for more than 10% — subject to AB 1482 and any local cap.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09. §827 notice thresholds confirmed; lease-survives-sale is settled property law.

entries.facts: The IRS $25,000 special allowance lets an owner deduct up to $25,000 of rental real-estate loss against ordinary income if they ACTIVELY participate (a lower bar than material participation — approving tenants, terms, and expenditures) and own at least 10%. The allowance is reduced by 50% of the amount by which modified AGI exceeds $100,000 and disappears at $150,000. Using a property manager does not disqualify active participation if the owner keeps genuine decision authority. Governed by IRC §469.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09 against IRS Pub 925 (2025) and Topic 425. $25k / $100k–$150k MAGI phaseout current.

entries.facts: Under IRC §1014, property inherited from a decedent generally takes a basis equal to its fair market value at the date of death (or the alternate valuation date), 'stepping up' the basis and erasing the built-in capital gain accrued during the decedent's life. This is why holding an appreciated rental until death can favor heirs over a lifetime sale.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09 against IRS Pub 551 (Rev. Dec 2025). FMV-at-death rule current.

sources.label: IRS Publication 551, Basis of Assets

entries.facts: The FHA Section 203(b) program — FHA's most common owner-occupant mortgage insurance — allows about 96.5% financing, i.e., a minimum down payment of 3.5% for borrowers with qualifying credit. A 20% down payment is not required to buy an owner-occupied home.

entries.facts: Residential policies include Coverage D (Loss of Use): renters policies pay Additional Living Expenses (temporary housing such as a hotel, meals, storage) when a covered peril makes the unit uninhabitable; landlord/dwelling policies pay 'fair rental value' (lost rent) in the same situation. Coverage depends on the policy and on the peril being covered. A standard California residential lease has no mechanism to bill a tenant a separate insurance surcharge (unlike a commercial NNN lease); insurance cost is recovered through rent, subject to the AB 1482 cap.

entries.facts: California Proposition 103 (1988) established a 'prior approval' system under which the Insurance Commissioner must approve a property/casualty insurance rate before an insurer may use it (Insurance Code §§1861.01–1861.16, with the rate standard at §1861.05). It is often invoked in debates about why California insurance availability and pricing have tightened.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09 against CA Dept. of Insurance Prop 103 page.

sources.label: California Dept. of Insurance — Proposition 103 Intervenor Program

entries.facts: Owner-occupied mortgages carry lower rates than investment/non-owner-occupied loans because Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac apply risk-based Loan-Level Price Adjustments (LLPAs) to investment-property loans (roughly 1.125% to 4.125% depending on LTV) while principal residences get the most favorable pricing. Higher default risk on investor loans translates into higher rates.
entries.currencyNote: Verified 2026-07-09 against Fannie Mae LLPA Matrix and Selling Guide occupancy guidance.
